findings.summary: The block shows `$ vloop doctor` followed by the four n/a rows in a row, as if that were the whole output. Doctor does not print them together. With every agent on copilot, other rows come between them: second review and the copilot rows after claude, the plan rows after trust, copilot plugin after plugin. A doctor: summary line comes last. A test copied from the block as literal output fails, and a gate that greps for four consecutive lines fails too.
findings.evidence: internal/cli/doctor.go:116 (claude), :118-130 (doctorSecondReview, copilot rows when copilot keys exist), :132-136 (trust), :138-139 (plan rows), :141-145 (plugin), :147-152 (copilot plugin), :154-158 (gate edits); :85 prints the doctor: summary.
findings.fix: Write the command as `vloop doctor | grep 'no session in use runs on claude'`, followed by the four lines in that order. Or say that the four rows are shown among the others, in this order.

findings.section: Behaviour contract — L1 (resolution: 'when it sets the key'; 'A list key takes the whole list of the layer that wins')
findings.summary: The contract does not say whether an empty list in the local file (for example `metrics.code = []`) sets the key. Today an empty array in the shared file does not set it: the value stays the default. If that rule carries over, a developer cannot clear a shared list on their machine. `config set --local metrics.code ''` removes the key and cannot write an empty list. A session will choose one reading.
findings.evidence: internal/config/config.go:340-370: resolveList calls set(text, SourceFile) only when len(names) > 0, so an empty array falls through to the default; config.go:631-633 and :660-663: '' removes the key.
findings.fix: Add one line to L1. Either 'an empty list in the local file is treated as in the shared file: it does not set the key, so a shared list cannot be emptied locally' or 'an empty list in the local file sets the key to empty, overriding the shared list'. Then pin it in a test.

decisions: Precedence is environment, then local file, then shared file, then default. Sound; C-1's meaning of the environment is kept.
The local file is .vloop/config.local.toml, beside the shared file, following the *.local.* convention. Sound.

Any key may be set locally, never [[check]]; a list key is replaced, not merged. Sound. This includes keys that shape committed output or safety (metrics.*, areas, language, run.gate-scratch, run.git-config-ignore, run.verify, run.second-review), and nothing in the run's records says a value came from the local file. Consider logging the local keys in the run log; the brief does not.
The run refuses a local file that git would commit, tracked or un-ignored, rather than the driver leaving it out of its commits. Sound: only the refusal also protects interactive commits.
The local file is a session input: the input guard and the five fences gain it; plan.json and the Copilot hook do not change. Sound (plan.json has no config.toml entry today either).
One brief covers L1–L5. Acceptable; L5 is independent but small.
'Claude in use' mirrors copilotKeys; doctor also counts agent.review-brief and run does not; an unreadable config counts as in use. Sound.
When Claude is not in use, the four rows are n/a with the message 'no session in use runs on claude'. When Claude is in use and claude is missing, plugin and gate edits keep today's empty n/a. Fine.

copilot.credit-usd goes from 0.0066667 to 0.01. It rests on GitHub's billing page as the author read it on 2026-11-20, which is not in the repository and which I could not check (no web). The operator should confirm the figures. The literal value is in the contract, so sessions do not need the page.

Decided here: the [[check]] refusal applies on every command that reads config; an empty or unknown-keys-only local file gets ✓; the ignore test asks about the path itself (global excludes count); the config set notice goes to stderr. All reasonable.
Left implicit: the config.local overrides warning never stops a run; `config set --local` prints no notice when an environment variable overrides the key it writes. Worth an explicit yes.
Starting point: the run branch starts from main plus the README branch (efde799d) plus the ready commit. That is the operator's call, and this checkout already sits on efde799d.

Acceptance 1 runs plan and gate review on Copilot, which README.md:96-97 says are not yet qualified. The brief only promises to get past the preflight ('for the preflight only'). The operator should know it does not qualify them.
